title: Physics 2: Electricity, Magnetism, Waves & Optics
subject: Electromagnetism
summary: Calculus-based electricity and magnetism from Coulomb to Maxwell, then mechanical waves, sound, geometric and wave optics. Prepares for Griffiths-level E&M and for quantum mechanics; chemistry hooks include molecular dipoles, dielectrics, the Hall effect and mass spectrometry, NMR magnetic moments, the EM spectrum, polarimetry and X-ray diffraction.

Estimate the field amplitudes in sunlight or a laser beam given its intensity.

objectives: Order the regions of the EM spectrum by wavelength, frequency, photon energy and typical sources, and match them to spectroscopic techniques (NMR radio, IR vibrational, UV-Vis electronic).
Convert among wavelength, frequency, wavenumber (cm^-1) and photon energy (eV, kJ/mol).

units.title: Mechanical Waves & Sound
units.summary: Travelling and standing waves, wave speed, energy, interference, beats, sound and the Doppler effect; the wave equation and mode ideas carried into optics and quantum mechanics.

lessons.title: Describing Travelling Waves
objectives: Describe a travelling wave y(x,t) = A sin(kx - omega t + phi) and relate wavelength, wave number, frequency, period and phase speed.
Distinguish transverse and longitudinal waves and identify the direction of particle motion versus the direction of propagation.

lessons.title: The Wave Equation & Speed on a String
objectives: Show that any function f(x - vt) satisfies the 1D wave equation and derive the equation for a string.
Derive the wave speed on a stretched string v = sqrt(T/mu).

objectives: Compute the energy and power carried by a sinusoidal wave on a string, scaling as A^2 omega^2.
Explain how reflection from fixed and free ends changes the phase of a pulse.

Add two waves of the same frequency analytically and with phasors.

objectives: Describe a complex vibration as a sum of normal modes (harmonic series) with Fourier ideas.

objectives: Relate pressure and displacement amplitudes in a sound wave and compute the speed of sound in a gas from thermal properties.
Compute intensity and the decibel level and apply the inverse-square law.

objectives: Compute the beat frequency of two close frequencies and explain it as interference in time.
Apply the Doppler formula for moving source and/or observer and describe a shock wave (Mach cone).

units.title: Light, Reflection, Refraction & Imaging
units.summary: Light as a ray: reflection, refraction, total internal reflection, dispersion, and image formation with mirrors, lenses and simple optical instruments.

lessons.title: Reflection, Refraction & the Index of Refraction
objectives: State the laws of reflection and Snell's law, and derive Snell's law from the wave picture via Huygens's principle (or Fermat's principle).
Compute the speed and wavelength of light in a medium and relate refractive index to polarisability.

lessons.title: Total Internal Reflection & Dispersion
objectives: Compute critical angle and explain total internal reflection in fibre optics and prisms.
Explain dispersion (n depends on wavelength) and the formation of a rainbow qualitatively.

lessons.title: Mirrors, Thin Lenses & Image Formation
objectives: Locate and characterise (real/virtual, upright/inverted, magnification) images formed by plane and spherical mirrors using the mirror equation and ray diagrams.
Apply the thin-lens equation and lensmaker's formula to converging and diverging lenses.

lessons.title: Two-Lens Instruments & the Eye
objectives: Analyse a two-lens system (microscope or telescope) and compute its angular magnification.
Describe the eye and common vision defects in terms of lens power in diopters.

units.title: Interference & Diffraction
units.summary: Double-slit and thin-film interference, interferometers, single-slit and grating diffraction, and resolution; X-ray diffraction of crystals is the chemist's structural probe.

lessons.title: Double-Slit Interference & Coherence
objectives: Derive the double-slit bright-fringe condition d sin(theta) = m lambda and the intensity pattern I = I0 cos^2(delta/2).
Explain coherence and why independent light sources do not show stable fringes.

lessons.title: Thin Films & the Michelson Interferometer
objectives: Compute the conditions for constructive and destructive interference in a thin film, including the phase change on reflection.
Describe the Michelson interferometer and use it to measure a small displacement or wavelength.

lessons.title: Single-Slit Diffraction, Missing Orders & Gratings
objectives: Derive the single-slit minima a sin(theta) = m lambda and the intensity envelope I = I0 (sin(beta)/beta)^2.
Combine interference and diffraction to find missing orders in a double-slit pattern.
Use a diffraction grating to determine wavelengths and compute resolving power.

objectives: Apply the Rayleigh criterion for a circular aperture and estimate the resolution of an eye or telescope.
Use Bragg's law to relate X-ray diffraction angles to crystal plane spacings.
